summary: Mt. Hood NF summit lookout: crow's nest 1925, 40-ft L-4 tower 1934, windstorm 1959, R-6 tower 1962, gone by 1971; a hiking blog reports summit communication buildings.

facts.design: L-4 (40-foot pole tower, 1934); the final 1962 tower was a 41-foot R-6 flat-cab
facts.status_note: Last tower gone by 1971 (removed or burned, sources differ); a hiking blog reports communication buildings still stand on the summit

access.note: Hiking trail from Starvation Creek Trailhead; northern and western flanks lie in the Mark O. Hatfield Wilderness

visit.trail_note: About 6 miles from Starvation Creek Trailhead, gaining 5,000 feet; the trail had recently reopened after the 2017 Eagle Creek Fire

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A January 1924 item says a ranger established a lookout station during 1923; firetower.org, firelookout.com and a hiking blog date the first crow's nest and tent to 1925. The story gives both.

firetower.org, firelookout.com and the hiking blog say the 1952 tower was destroyed in the 1959 windstorm. The Oregon lookouts history says the lookout was severely damaged and the cabin wrecked, and a February 1960 entry there planned a new cabin on the 40-foot tower.
Firetower.org, firelookout.com and the blog say the 1962 tower was removed or gone by 1971; the Oregon lookouts history says it was burned during the winter of 1971.
firetower.org describes a 40-foot pole tower; the Oregon lookouts history describes a 40-foot timber tower.

sources.title: 3 Popular Hikes That Are Former Fire Lookout Sites

notes_for_editor: Today's summit description rests on one hiking blog (The Roaming Civic); no Forest Service or recent photo source was found, so treat the communication buildings as unconfirmed. The brief's design L-4 and height 12.2 m describe the 1934 40-foot tower; the final 1962 tower was a 41-foot R-6 flat-cab, about 12.5 m, which the record does not list, so the design field notes it rather than replacing the earlier design. The brief's elevation (1511.8 m for the site) was not checked; Wikipedia gives the peak as 5,010 ft (1,527 m). Access marked public because the hiking route is a listed trail; the 2017 Eagle Creek Fire closure has since reopened per the blog. Checked 2026-10-09: the 1960 'letter' is a dated entry (February 4, 1960) in the Oregon lookouts history; the 1962 claim no longer cites the hiking blog, which has no 1962 quote.
